items.title: One current truth, kept by code
items.summary: What is current and what is retired lives in ONE registry. A retired concept is data: a pattern, the context in which naming it is still true, and the truth that replaced it. The same scan runs on every push, in the test suite, in the rehearsal and on every episode.

evidence.source: Gloaguen et al., Evaluating AGENTS.md, arXiv 2602.11988
evidence.finding: agents obey repository context files; such files do not generally raise success and raise cost by more than 20%, so a wrong or long file is a direct loss

evidence.source: Chroma, Context Rot (Hong, Troynikov, Huber)
evidence.finding: reliability falls as input grows; distractors close in topic to the answer hurt most

items.title: Reference docs are rendered from the code, never typed
items.summary: The system reference is generated from the live code (facts, checks, settings, jobs, tabs, modules). A test fails when the committed file differs, so a doc can not state a number the code does not hold.

evidence.source: Grafana Loki CI step: check generated documentation
evidence.finding: CI fails when generated reference docs differ from the committed file

evidence.source: Fern, Stopping schema drift
evidence.finding: derive docs from one definition; treat drift as a build failure

items.title: History is archived whole and marked, never deleted, never followed
items.summary: A replaced document moves to the archive folder under a first line that says it is historical and names what replaced it; the text under that line is left unedited. Current docs may name the archive only while saying it is history.

evidence.source: M. Fowler, Architecture Decision Record (bliki); Backstage ADR docs
evidence.finding: accepted records are never rewritten or deleted; they are superseded with a pointer to the replacement

items.title: Ratchet baseline for unavoidable mentions
items.summary: Code that must name an old value (a one-time setting move) is listed in a baseline by file and rule, with a count and a reason. One more hit fails; one fewer also fails until the entry is pruned. The list can only shrink.

evidence.source: ESLint, Introducing bulk suppressions
evidence.finding: baseline existing violations by count per file and rule; report new ones at once; prune stale suppressions

items.title: The build chat's rule file is short, and wording is not enforcement
items.summary: The rule file a build chat loads holds only the non-obvious rules of this codebase and stays under 200 lines. Every rule that matters also has a check, because a context file is context, not enforcement.

evidence.source: Anthropic, Claude Code memory docs
evidence.finding: target under 200 lines; specific and concise instructions are followed more reliably; CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration

evidence.source: Gloaguen et al., Evaluating AGENTS.md, arXiv 2602.11988
evidence.finding: repository overviews do not help; only non-standard practices are worth writing

items.title: B1 build takeaway: scan what the code says about itself
items.summary: Generating the system doc from the code and then scanning it found stale statements inside LIVE settings notes that no search of the docs folder could find. Scan what the code says about itself, not only the documents. Keep current docs one fact per line: the rules are line-based.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B1
evidence.finding: first scan: 33 retired-concept hits + 11 dead paths across the rule file, ledger, build prompt, Mission Control guide and 5 settings notes; after B1: 0

items.title: Executing a decision means retiring what it replaces
items.summary: When a decision replaces a value, register the old value as a retired concept BEFORE searching by hand. The scan found a fourth viewer line with the old cadence that a manual search had missed, and the generated system doc is what exposed the ledger-versus-code mismatch in the first place.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B1b
evidence.finding: manual search found 3 of 4 lines; the retired rule found the 4th on its first run

items.title: Knowledge leaves the Palace through one guarded doorway
items.summary: Every playbook is built by one function whose first step is the status-and-date guard. A retired, superseded, expired or merely proposed item can never reach a prompt, whatever label it carries: memory systems that only LABEL a revoked fact keep serving it.

evidence.source: Shen, Toyoda, Leung, Revoked but Still Authoritative, arXiv 2609.08258
evidence.finding: five soft-revocation memory systems, 9 scenarios x 9 models: no system enforces revocation by default; a visible revoked record is returned, outranks its replacement and leads the agent to act on it; a guard that withholds it fixes this

items.title: Withdrawn knowledge takes its descendants with it
items.summary: When an item is retired or superseded, everything derived from it is sent back for re-validation by code in the same call. Readers are never trusted to check where a piece of knowledge came from: models rarely do.

evidence.source: Nakayashiki, When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked, arXiv 2608.25553
evidence.finding: 16 models: a memory whose source had been withdrawn still drove the decision in 77.3 / 74.7 / 74.7% of episodes; provenance was inspected in about 1 episode in 5; a freshness cue did not help

items.title: Limits are served first and never vanish silently
items.summary: Limits - the owner's words, policy rules, failure lessons - come first in every playbook and hold a reserved share of it. A stale technique is dropped until re-validated; a stale limit keeps being served, marked review due, and is reported.

evidence.source: Nakayashiki, When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked, arXiv 2608.25553
evidence.finding: a one-sentence rule that prefers memories stating a limit recovered +89.3 points on decisions where the constraint limits the tempting action

items.title: Memory is itemised and merged by code, never rewritten by a model
items.summary: The organisation's memory is a set of small items changed by small merges in code. A model is never asked to rewrite the whole memory: that collapses it into a vague summary. Size is held by caps per kind that displace the lowest-value item.

evidence.source: Zhang et al., Agentic Context Engineering (ACE), arXiv 2510.04618, ICLR 2026
evidence.finding: itemised bullets + deterministic non-model delta merges: +10.6% on agent tasks, +8.6% finance, 86.9% lower adaptation latency; full rewrites cause context collapse; needs a reliable outcome signal

items.title: Nothing enters the Palace without dated evidence
items.summary: Every item needs at least one dated source, and its trust is computed by code from the kind of evidence. Text typed by viewers or found on the web is data: it never becomes an accepted item without assessment, and text that reads like an instruction to a model is refused.

evidence.source: Dash et al., From Untrusted Input to Trusted Memory (MPBench), arXiv 2606.04329
evidence.finding: one hostile memory write has long-term influence; 4 write channels, 9 structural weaknesses; agents that write and read memory more eagerly are more exploitable; prompt-injection defences do not cover it

items.title: A playbook is deterministic and named by its own text
items.summary: The same Palace state always gives a byte-identical playbook, and the playbook id is the hash of its text. The cached prompt prefix therefore survives until knowledge really changes, and the id is proof of exactly what a department was given.

evidence.source: Anthropic prompt-caching documentation
evidence.finding: a cache hit needs a 100% identical prefix; minimum cacheable length 512-4,096 tokens by model; cache reads cost 0.1x input or less

items.title: Keep everything, serve little
items.summary: Nothing is deleted - a replaced item is kept with a pointer to its successor - and each department gets only a small current slice under a hard cap, with the full record of any item fetched by id when it is needed.

evidence.source: Rasmussen et al., Zep: a temporal knowledge graph architecture for agent memory, arXiv 2501.13956
evidence.finding: contradicted facts are end-dated, not deleted; up to +18.5% accuracy and 90% lower latency on LongMemEval as context fell from about 115,000 to about 1,600 tokens

evidence.source: Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents
evidence.finding: find the smallest set of high-signal tokens; hybrid: preload a little, fetch the rest on demand

items.title: The life cycle of knowledge is data, and every move names who may make it
items.summary: An item is proposed, accepted, testing, proven or retired, superseded or expired. The legal moves are a table in code, each with the roles allowed to make it; the path is not a straight line, and an item earns 'proven' only from evidence of use measured by Growth & Learning.

evidence.source: Consortium for Service Innovation, KCS v6 Practices Guide, technique 5.2 (article states)
evidence.finding: Work in Progress / Not Validated / Validated / Archived; the life cycle is non-linear; an article is validated by successful reuse; archive instead of delete

items.title: Google Sheets limits shape the Palace index
items.summary: The Sheets API allows 300 requests a minute per project and 60 per user, advises payloads under 2 MB, and a cell holds 50,000 characters. So one index row carries everything a playbook needs (one read builds it), long bodies live outside the Sheet, and writes are batched.

evidence.source: Google Sheets API usage limits
evidence.finding: 300 read and 300 write requests a minute per project, 60 per user per project; 2 MB payload recommended; 180 s request timeout; HTTP 429 when exceeded

items.title: Small knowledge bases are ranked by tags and keywords in code
items.summary: For a few hundred short items, department, stage, tag and weighted keyword matching in code is enough: it costs nothing, is deterministic and adds no dependency. An embedding scorer is worth adding only if the Palace outgrows it or queries become paraphrase-heavy.

evidence.source: BM25 wins at scale (2026 scaling study, as reported; primary id not verified)
evidence.finding: keyword ranking beat dense retrieval and agent search on large corpora; at the smallest sizes exact matching with reasoning was enough

items.title: B2 build takeaway: read the real output, and make checkers accept anything
items.summary: Look at the real output of a selection rule on real data before trusting it: the first writers' playbook opened with a minor idea and left out the owner's core taste rule until priority and tighter addressing were added. And a checker must accept any input: the guard's own checker crashed on a retired row, and the audit trail hid outside edits until it ran first.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B2
evidence.finding: 39 new tests found 2 real bugs (the playbook checker raised on a retired row; upkeep logged its own changes before the audit compared hashes); 92 founding items, none refused, every applied_in reference resolves; a few low-priority limits do not fit an 1,800-token playbook for D1, D4, D12 and the Council (reported by the health check as a note)

items.title: The department contract is a state machine in code, with a proof per step
items.summary: The six steps of a department run (LOAD, ACT, EMIT, LEARN, EXECUTE, REPORT) are run and proven by code. No prompt asks a model to follow the steps, because multi-agent systems fail mostly on organisation, not on the model: repeated steps, unclear end conditions, missing verification.

evidence.source: Cemri et al., Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST), arXiv 2503.13657
evidence.finding: 1,600+ traces, 7 frameworks: step repetition 15.7%, reasoning-action mismatch 13.2%, unaware of termination conditions 12.4%, verification failures 23.5% together; a verification step gave +15.6%, prompt fixes were inconsistent

items.title: State changes on evidence that code observed, never on a claim
items.summary: A department cannot report its own progress and a memo cannot be closed by saying so. Receipts are built by the runner from what it observed (the playbook it loaded, ids the Sheet returned, money and model calls it counted); a memo closes only with a reference to proof that code can look up.

evidence.source: Wang et al., The Unreliable Progress Bar, arXiv 2609.08589
evidence.finding: models report their own task progress unreliably while work is under way; frameworks should not control task flow on the model's state reports alone

items.title: A handoff keeps the facts and loses the rules, so the rules are typed and never shortened
items.summary: A memo's audience is a typed list enforced by code when a department reads its inbox, and its constraints are printed whole every time a memo becomes prompt text. Only the body may be cut, and a cut is marked. A constraint that is too long is refused on write, never trimmed later.

evidence.source: Wang, Goyal, Chandrasekharan, Sundaram, Facts Without Rules: Boundary Metadata Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs, arXiv 2608.29028
evidence.finding: boundary survival fell from 0.80 to 0.57 under a 25-word handoff while facts stayed near ceiling; vague boundary wording leaked in 73% / 50% of cases, explicit constraints under 15%, a typed audience allowlist nearly zero

items.title: Deterministic verification with a coverage check catches most run failures at zero cost
items.summary: The runner recomputes what a run claims (cost, model calls, memo ids) and checks coverage: every inbound memo that was loaded must be dispositioned, every required department run must exist before a gate. Recomputing and coverage are code, cost nothing and raise no false alarm.

evidence.source: Dubey, Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures, arXiv 2608.02464
evidence.finding: a deterministic verification layer caught 60% of failures, 96% with a coverage check, with 0 false positives in 2,823 episodes; roll back and re-run recovered 45% against 16%

items.title: Departments are code around the existing calls: the organisation adds no model hop
items.summary: A department is a wrapper around work that already runs. Knowledge reaches a model inside the call that already exists (the cached layer of its system prompt), never through an extra orchestrated call. Splitting a procedure over more model calls raised failures in controlled tests and multiplies cost.

evidence.source: Dennis et al., In-Context Prompting Obsoletes Agent Orchestration for Procedural Tasks, arXiv 2604.27891
evidence.finding: an external orchestrator failed 9-24% of conversations against 0.5-11.5% for one prompt holding the whole procedure

evidence.source: Anthropic, How we built our multi-agent research system
evidence.finding: multi-agent runs use about 15x the tokens of a chat; resume from a checkpoint instead of restarting; pass artifacts by reference

items.cost_note: Rs 0: no model call is added by the department contract

items.title: A memo that asks for work states the objective, the end condition and the boundaries
items.summary: Every memo that asks a department to do something carries a one-line subject, a done_when that says what proves it is finished, and its constraints. Long material is stored once and linked, never copied through memos (a body over the size limit is refused).

evidence.source: Anthropic, How we built our multi-agent research system
evidence.finding: each delegated task needs an objective, an output format, guidance on tools and sources, and clear task boundaries; vague instructions led to duplicated work

items.title: Two clocks per memo, a ladder as data, bounded reminders
items.summary: Every memo has an acknowledge clock and a resolve clock. Acknowledging stops only the first. A miss climbs department, Council, owner. The owner hears about a stuck item once, then a bounded number of reminders, a few messages per pass at most; after that it rests on his list.

evidence.source: PagerDuty documentation, Escalation Policies (read 10 Nov 2026)
evidence.finding: not acknowledged inside the timeout -> the next rule; acknowledging stops escalation but does not resolve; a policy repeats at most 9 times and then stops notifying

items.title: Statuses and moves are data; a closed memo accepts nothing; the id is the request
items.summary: Memo statuses and the roles that may make each move are a table in code. A resolved or rejected memo accepts no further change: a recurrence is a new memo linked to the old one. The id is the hash of type, sender, audience and dedupe key, so writing the same memo twice is a no-op on a Sheet that has no transactions.

evidence.source: A2A Protocol specification 1.0.0, task states (read 10 Nov 2026)
evidence.finding: a task in a terminal state (completed, failed, canceled, rejected) accepts no further message; the sender's message id is used to detect duplicates

evidence.source: Richardson, Pattern: Transactional outbox, microservices.io (read 10 Nov 2026)
evidence.finding: a relay can publish a message more than once, so the consumer must be idempotent

items.title: A takeaway is measured, cannot score itself, and enters the Palace only when it is new
items.summary: The takeaway of a department run is built on what the run measured against the department's own earlier runs. It carries no score of its own. A confirmation is counted in the Takeaways tab; only a deviation, a failed check or a failure is proposed to the Palace, as proposed, and the same class of finding updates one item.

evidence.source: Yin et al., From Reflection to Co-Evolution: Self-Evolving Agents with Locally Verified Memory (Anchor), arXiv 2611.10382
evidence.finding: most self-written lessons barely change a decision and some reinforce the wrong action; admitting only verified ones gave up to +19.9% success with 41% fewer stored memories

evidence.source: Asadolahi et al., Memory Reward Inflation in Self-Improving LLM Agents, arXiv 2608.00017
evidence.finding: self-graded memories inflate and a judge whose errors correlate with the self-grading cannot correct them

items.title: Strict before the work, never throw the work away after it
items.summary: LOAD raises before any work or money. After ACT a failed step never raises in a production wrapper: the result is returned, the run is recorded as a breach, and the episode gate holds the video. A raise after the upload step would lose the video id and make the retry upload a second copy.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B3
evidence.finding: the upload id is written to the Sheet only after the upload call returns; an exception between the two leaves no record, so a retry would upload again - found by reading whatifs/episode.py before wrapping it

items.title: Escalation never waits on a department that cannot act
items.summary: The escalation ladder skips any holder that has no wired run, read from the registry by code. A memo to a department that is not built yet goes straight to the next level that can act, so nothing waits on an empty chair; when the department is wired it joins the ladder without any other change.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B3
evidence.finding: 8 of 15 departments have no run of their own after B3; without the skip every memo to them would sit for its whole deadline before anyone saw it

items.title: B3 build takeaway: read the production path before wrapping it, and test the silence
items.summary: Reading the upload path before wrapping it changed the design: a raise after the upload would have caused a second upload, so the runner is strict before the work and never throws work away after it. And test what happens when nothing happens: the first deadline test showed a stuck memo reaching the owner's level without any message being sent.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B3
evidence.finding: 99 new tests found 3 real bugs in the new code: a stuck memo at the owner's level sent no message (wrong default), a department's own breach memo blocked its next run (coverage check), a measure function crashed on odd output (would have held a healthy video). Live proof: one unwrapped call site + stock takeaways accepted -> 10 tests failed and the real pipeline held the episode at the script gate.

items.title: One green run proves one seed: sweep the fake pipeline over fixed episode ids
items.summary: The fake pipeline is seeded by the episode id, so a single green rehearsal proves one id. Before a batch is accepted, tools/sweep.py runs the whole pipeline over fixed ids, one process per id, and every hold, crash and warning class is traced to its cause. A red run is reproduced with its own id, never re-run until it passes.

evidence.source: Dutta et al., Detecting Flaky Tests in Probabilistic and Machine Learning Applications (FLASH), ISSTA 2020
evidence.finding: running tests under many random seeds exposed 11 new flaky tests in 20 projects that single-seed runs had not shown

evidence.source: Dutta et al., To Seed or Not to Seed? An Empirical Analysis of Usage of Seeds for Testing in Machine Learning Projects, ICST 2022
evidence.finding: in 114 projects, fixing one seed was used as a workaround that hides the failing seeds instead of fixing their cause

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B0b (baseline re-check)
evidence.finding: GitHub run 38 (red at the rehearsal step) was reproduced on the old code with the episode id of that minute, EP202611101111: held by promise_paid at 44.7 s; the ids of the two following minutes passed

items.title: A test that skips proves nothing: GitHub's Checks fail on any skipped test
items.summary: A skipped test is not a passed test. On GitHub's Checks one skipped test fails the run and is named. A check that depends on the machine must be made to run there or be removed, never left skipping.

evidence.source: Kim, Chen et al., How Disabled Tests Manifest in Test Maintainability Challenges?, ESEC/FSE 2021
evidence.finding: in 122,000 commits of 15 systems, 41% of disabled tests were never brought back and most stayed disabled for years

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B0b (baseline re-check)
evidence.finding: the comparison with the reference frames of the base renderer skipped on every machine (laptop and GitHub) because of a library-version guard; forced to run it failed in 36 of 36 frames: the particle layer, on by default, had changed the picture and nobody saw it. One more test looked for a folder that exists nowhere

items.title: Tests must measure the library versions that make the videos
items.summary: Every workflow installs a pinned package with the bounds of requirements.txt, and a test fails when the installed or imported version on the test machine is outside them. A green check on another major version of a library says nothing about production.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B0b (baseline re-check)
evidence.finding: GitHub's Checks installed OpenCV without bounds and ran 5.0.0 while production pins it below 5; with 5.0.0 all 36 reference frames of the base renderer differ. Found by the first run whose failures were written onto the public run page

evidence.source: Flutter project, Writing a golden file test (contributor guide)
evidence.finding: reference images are generated and compared on one defined platform because renderer and library differences change pixels

items.title: Built but never wired does not exist: no unread Settings cell, unused tab or uncalled function
items.summary: A Settings cell nothing reads, a Sheet tab nothing uses and a function nothing calls are promises nothing keeps. The truth registry scans for all three on every push and on every episode; the ones that never worked are listed with what is true and marked NOT ACTIVE, and the lists may only shrink.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B0b (baseline re-check)
evidence.finding: of 691 Settings cells 8 were read by no code in any version ever pushed, among them the effort alignment for cached prefixes (its function was tested but never called) and the blind test of the writers' room against a single prompt (never built, switched ON by default); 2 of 78 tabs and 10 of 1,404 functions were used by no production code, among them the check of the character bible

items.title: A red check must name its cause where everyone can read it
items.summary: The Checks workflow writes the failed tests, the skipped tests, the failed contract checks with their reason and the episode ids onto the public run page, and the totals when green. A red run is then diagnosed without a sign-in and reproduced with its id.

evidence.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow commands for GitHub Actions (error and notice annotations, job summaries)
evidence.finding: an error or notice command creates an annotation on the run; a step can append Markdown to the job summary; at most 20 step summaries are shown per job

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B0b (baseline re-check)
evidence.finding: the first run with annotations showed in one glance what no batch had seen before: 27 tests red for one cause, the library version printed in the message

items.title: B0b build takeaway: ask of every check where it really runs and what reads every promise
items.summary: A baseline is not proven by its own green lights. Ask of every check on which machine and library version it really runs and whether it can skip; ask of every setting, tab and function what reads, uses or calls it. Make the failure visible in public first: the first visible red run found more than every green one before it.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B0b (baseline re-check)
evidence.finding: The sweep of 40 fixed episode ids was green on every id, and the faults were found elsewhere: the reference-frame comparison had never run on any machine (the particle layer had changed all 36 frames unseen); GitHub's Checks were measuring OpenCV 5.0.0 while production pins it below 5 (shown by the first run whose failures were written onto the public run page); 8 Settings cells, 2 tabs and 10 functions had never been wired, among them a paid test that was switched on by default and never built. GitHub run 38 was explained by reproducing it with the episode id of its minute.

items.title: A change counts only when later evidence shows that it took effect
items.summary: A ticket is not done when the change is written. It is done when rows another component wrote AFTER it show the effect: a later department run that was served the item, a video made after the change that passed the lever's checks, the features of later videos, GitHub's checks on the merge commit. The engine's own read-back is never enough.

evidence.source: Mohammadi et al., Atomix: Timely, Transactional Tool Use for Reliable Agentic Workflows, arXiv 2602.14849 (abstract)
evidence.finding: orchestrators that treat a tool's return as the signal that work is settled leave partial effects, stale writes and irreversible sends; a change is committed only when nothing earlier can still conflict

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B4 (Execution Engine)
evidence.finding: the first version verified an updated item with a playbook that still held the OLD text of the same item; proof now names the exact item version

items.title: At one video a week, isolate a change instead of testing it statistically
items.summary: A setting or an experiment changes between videos, never under a script already written, and a department has ONE unverified change at a time. Then the checks of one video can be attributed to one change. With no evidence inside the window the change is rolled back: the earlier value was the known-good state.

evidence.source: LaunchDarkly documentation, Guarded rollouts and regression detection
evidence.finding: automatic rollback needs a minimum sample before any decision; with too few samples at the end of a rollout it rolls back; it suits metrics where worse is unambiguous

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B4 (Execution Engine)
evidence.finding: the end-to-end test: a setting ticket waited while the first fake video was made, was applied at the next tick and verified by the second video's retention check

items.title: Rollback restores the old value only if the cell still holds what the engine wrote
items.summary: Rolling back is compare-and-swap. If the owner typed another value into the Sheet after the engine's change, that value stays and the ledger says so. A faithful restore of old state next to newer facts creates a combination that never existed.

evidence.source: Wu et al., Safe to Resume? Breaking Execution Continuity of Agent Execution via Rollback, arXiv 2608.29381 (abstract)
evidence.finding: correct rollback does not imply secure recovery: a restored checkpoint can resume next to external effects and assumptions that never coexisted with it; three end-to-end attacks across five frameworks

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B4 (Execution Engine)
evidence.finding: test: the owner's hand-typed 12 survived the rollback of the engine's 10; the ledger row reads rollback_skipped

items.title: Inside its range the direction of a lever decides who may turn it
items.summary: The organisation's own values are checked like untrusted input: registered lever, owner department, type, range, one step at a time - refused, never clamped. A department may move a lever in the direction that makes a gate stricter or cheaper; the direction that weakens a gate, costs more or changes the owner's plan waits for his one tap.

evidence.source: Cloudflare, post-mortem of the outage of 18 November 2025
evidence.finding: an internally generated configuration file doubled in size, hit a hard limit in the proxy and failed the network for 5 h 46 min; first remediation: harden the ingestion of internally generated configuration the same way as user input

evidence.source: Google Cloud, incident report of 12 June 2025 (Service Control)
evidence.finding: a policy with blank fields replicated worldwide in seconds into a code path with no flag and no error handling; remediation: incremental roll-out with time to validate

items.title: A code build merges by itself only when its real diff adds new tests and nothing else
items.summary: The automatic merge is decided by code reading the real diff, never by the request or the builder's word: new files tests/test_*.py only, nothing deleted, at least one new test, a bounded size, every check green. Anything else goes to the owner with the reason. The step in which the builder reads the spec holds no Sheet, WhatsApp or merge credential.

evidence.source: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents, arXiv 2605.21384
evidence.finding: a coding agent passed 97.8% of the visible tests and 83.3% of the held-out tests; the gap of 14.5 points grows with the size of the task

evidence.source: The Hacker News, Claude Code GitHub Action flaw (fixed in v1.0.94)
evidence.finding: injected text could make the agent read the job's environment and leak its credentials; a job that reads untrusted text should hold no credential beyond the model's and the workflow's own

items.title: A ticket is one change the engine can compile: lever class, target, value
items.summary: A = knowledge: target palace:<key>, value the item (or empty to accept a proposed one), from the Council. B = setting: target the Settings cell, to the department that owns it. C = experiment: target playbook:<showrunner|writer|packager|director|reel>, value rule, metric, source_url. D = rule: as A with a style or policy rule. E = code: to D12, value spec, files, tests_to_add.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B4 (Execution Engine)
evidence.finding: each form is compiled by whatifs/org/execute.py and refused with the reason when it does not fit (tests/test_v12_exec.py: one refusal test per rule)

items.title: B4 build takeaway: ask of every proof who wrote it and when, and of every wait who is told
items.summary: Ask of every 'verified' who wrote the evidence and when: the first engine accepted a playbook that still held the OLD text of an item. Ask of every waiting state when its clock ends and who hears of it. And prove a wiring by running the real job: a scan that counts names cannot see a call with a common name being removed.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B4 (Execution Engine)
evidence.finding: Six faults were found by tests and by re-reading the finished code, none by the first green run: an updated item was 'verified' by a playbook holding its old version; a video that began in the second of a change did not count as made after it; a ticket for a department that only runs inside a video would have waited a week and climbed to the owner for a missed acknowledgement; a merge whose checks never reported would have been reverted on a guess; removing the engine's call from the tick job left every guard green; a shell here-document halved the backslashes of a patch and reformatted a whole data file.

items.title: A research source counts only when the search tool returned it, it resolves and it is dated
items.summary: Evidence comes from the search API's own citation blocks, never the model's prose. A URL the search never returned is a phantom: dropped, counted, minus two points of ceiling. A source must resolve and carry a publication date not in the future; its type is set by its domain. A finding whose sources all fail is dropped; a question with nothing left writes no memo.

evidence.source: Rao, Wong, Callison-Burch, Detecting and Correcting Reference Hallucinations in Commercial LLMs and Deep Research Agents, arXiv 2604.03173 (abstract)
evidence.finding: 3-13% of citation URLs were hallucinated and 5-18% did not resolve; deep research agents cited more and hallucinated more; a liveness check cut non-resolving URLs 6-79x to under 1%

evidence.source: Onweller et al., Cited but Not Verified, arXiv 2605.06635 (abstract)
evidence.finding: link validity above 94% and relevance above 80%, yet only 39-77% factual accuracy; accuracy fell about 42% as tool calls grew from 2 to 150

items.title: Judges answer yes or no to fixed questions; code turns the answers into scores and the verdict
items.summary: Asked for 1-10 scores, model judges inflate. The Board's judges answer fixed yes/no questions with a one-line reason each (evidence, novelty, impact, feasibility, risk); code turns the share of yes into scores, caps evidence at what code verified, scores cost from the rupees and applies the verdict table. An unanswered question counts against the memo.

evidence.source: Huang and Zhou, Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Based Review Paradigms for Academic Paper Quality Assessment, arXiv 2610.41391 (abstract)
evidence.finding: direct absolute rating compressed most predictions above the accept threshold and flagged almost none of the weak papers

evidence.source: Lee et al., CheckEval, arXiv 2403.18771 (EMNLP 2025)
evidence.finding: decomposed binary checklist questions raised average agreement across 12 evaluator models by 0.45 and reduced score variance

items.title: Balance the jury by model family, read every memo in two orders, and let the other family veto
items.summary: Judges prefer their own model family and flip with the reading order. The Board has one strong judge per family (no cheap fallback), each reading the memos in two orders; scores are the mean of family means, and the family that did NOT write a memo must earn the same verdict alone. A judge answered by the wrong family or a cheap model is not counted; under two families = no verdict.

evidence.source: Awuni et al., Who Judges Matters: Measuring Family-Conditioned Preference in LLM-as-Judge Panels, arXiv 2609.17857 (abstract)
evidence.finding: every family preferred its own by 3.4-8.4 points; 55.4% of AB/BA pairs reversed with the order; panel composition changed 18.5% of outcomes

evidence.source: Verga et al., Replacing Judges with Juries (PoLL), arXiv 2404.18796 (abstract)
evidence.finding: a panel of models from disjoint families beat a single large judge with less intra-model bias at over 7x lower cost

items.title: Plant a memo that must be rejected in every review session; a jury that passes it is void
items.summary: Inflation is the default failure of model judges. Every Board session hides one memo built by code to fail (no or irrelevant evidence, a guaranteed-views claim, a policy breach) among the real ones. Each model family must reject it on its own, or the session writes no verdict, the memos wait and a problem memo records it. Calibration is measured every session, not assumed.

evidence.source: LLM-as-a-Reviewer benchmark, arXiv 2605.25415 (search summary)
evidence.finding: most of 12 models over-rated papers, some families by up to 2.43 points on the venue scale

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B5 (R&D + Review Board)
evidence.finding: a judge that answers yes to every good question and no to every risk question passes no canary: the session is void and no assessment is written (tested)

items.title: Only facts can be accepted from research; a creative idea is at most a test with a pre-registered prediction
items.summary: What a jury loves before execution falls hardest after it. The Board may accept only facts (platform policy, tools and prices, re-validated Palace facts) with strong evidence. An idea is at most a test, and only with a prediction code can measure: a contract check or an Analytics column, a direction and a horizon in videos - the experiment's metric once the Council decides.

evidence.source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang, The Ideation-Execution Gap, arXiv 2506.20803 (ICLR 2026)
evidence.finding: 43 experts executed ideas blind; LLM ideas scored higher before execution and dropped significantly more after it on every metric, with rankings flipping

items.title: Research what is failing us, not what is trending
items.summary: The research agenda is computed by code at no cost from our own gaps: failed promises, the weakest breakout component, recurring problems, the owner's open instructions (asked first, even past the cap), outlier videos, expiring Palace facts, new models and a standing policy question. A question is not asked again for RESEARCH_REPEAT_DAYS unless its gap persists.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B5 (R&D + Review Board)
evidence.finding: the agenda draws on eight gap sources; failed organisation checks are excluded as code faults; a question never re-opens while its last memo is still open (tested)

evidence.source: Anthropic web search tool documentation
evidence.finding: USD 10 per 1,000 searches plus tokens; max_uses caps searches per turn; citations carry url, title and up to 150 characters of cited text

items.title: YouTube does not pay for mass-produced or repetitive videos: every video must differ in substance
items.summary: Since 15 July 2025 YouTube's monetisation policy calls it inauthentic content: uploads that are mass-produced or repetitive, such as narrated stories with only superficial differences, are not eligible. AI tools are allowed. Every proposal is asked whether it could make our videos repetitive; R&D re-checks this policy every 28 days.

evidence.source: YouTube Help, YouTube channel monetization policies (inauthentic content update, via TeamYouTube)
evidence.finding: content that is mass-produced or repetitive is not eligible for monetisation; the update renamed the repetitious content policy to inauthentic content

items.title: B5 build takeaway: make every judgement a pure function the check can re-run, and plant a test the judge must fail
items.summary: Scores, the verdict and the evidence ceiling are pure functions of stored data, so check research_cadence re-computes them and a typed or forged verdict fails. A jury is trusted only after it rejects a memo built to be rejected. And every new wiring gets a test that runs the real job: removing the research round from the learning job left both name scans green.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B5 (R&D + Review Board)
evidence.finding: Seven faults were found by re-reading and by tests, none by the first green run: the ceiling counted a source no finding used; a re-asked question would have collided with its open memo; a question whose run died stayed 'asked' forever; a failed call waited 28 days; the recomputed ceiling could differ at midnight; a broken weekly run would have been re-paid daily; an accepted assessment would have told the owner it was 'stuck'.

items.title: Knowledge counts as used only when a quote from the work proves it
items.summary: A model's list of the ideas it used proves nothing: citations can be correct yet never used. Every creative call cites the playbook lines it applied with a 4-30 word quote from its own answer; code finds the quote in the final output. Ids never offered and quotes not found are kept for the record and never counted.

evidence.source: Wallat, Heuss, de Rijke, Anand, Correctness is not Faithfulness in RAG Attributions, arXiv 2412.18004 (ICTIR 2025)
evidence.finding: up to 57% of citations unfaithful (post-rationalised) in adversarial tests

evidence.source: Saxena et al., Generation-Time vs. Post-hoc Citation, arXiv 2509.21557 (NeurIPS 2025 workshop)
evidence.finding: citing while generating wins on precision, citing afterwards on coverage; retrieval quality drives both

items.title: Put the playbook at an edge of the prompt, outside the cached layers, and keep it small
items.summary: Models use what sits at the start or end of a prompt and lose what sits in the middle; every model gets less reliable as input grows; even the best follow only about two thirds of 500 instructions. The playbook sits at the END of the system prompt, never mid-brief and outside the cached layers (inside them it re-wrote the cache per task), under a hard cap: limits, canon, then proven knowledge.

evidence.source: Liu et al., Lost in the Middle, TACL 12 (2024) 157-173
evidence.finding: U-shaped accuracy by position of the relevant text

evidence.source: Hong, Troynikov, Huber, Context Rot, Chroma technical report
evidence.finding: 18 models get less reliable as input length grows; distractors hurt more with length

evidence.source: How Many Instructions Can LLMs Follow at Once? (IFScale), arXiv 2507.11538
evidence.finding: best frontier models about 68% accurate at 500 instructions; earlier instructions favoured

items.title: Re-state the cast and the knowledge in every creative call, not once
items.summary: A system prompt's grip fades within a few turns of a long exchange. The playbook with the cast canon is put into EVERY creative call of a run (showrunner, bible, each draft, each rewrite, the punch-up), so a character never drifts away from who they are halfway through the room.

evidence.source: Li et al., Measuring and Controlling Instruction (In)Stability in Language Model Dialogs, arXiv 2402.10962 (COLM 2024)
evidence.finding: significant persona drift within eight rounds of conversation

items.title: The show's history is written by code from its own records, and becomes canon only on air
items.summary: Long generated stories get facts and timelines wrong, most in the middle. So the canon is not the model's memory: after every script, code records the case (charge, verdict, style, deciding detail, witness twist, Grimm's prototype, the promised next case); the record becomes canon when the platform confirms the upload.

evidence.source: ConStory-Bench, Lost in Stories: Consistency Bugs in Long Story Generation by LLMs, arXiv 2603.05890 (ACL Findings 2026)
evidence.finding: consistency errors most common in factual and temporal dimensions, mostly mid-narrative

evidence.source: Finding Flawed Fictions, arXiv 2504.11900 (COLM 2025)
evidence.finding: LLM-written stories carry 50-100% more plot holes than human originals

evidence.source: Park et al., Generative Agents, arXiv 2304.03442 (UIST 2023)
evidence.finding: memory, reflection and planning each critical to believability (ablations)

items.title: Every case calls back to the last one in one spoken line
items.summary: Attachment to characters grows with repeated exposure and with being spoken to. Each script pays a continuity debt: one spoken line that calls back to the newest aired case, changed a little each time (a running gag that never changes stops being noticed; one that changes too much stops being recognised). Code finds the line in the final script.

evidence.source: University of Essex, parasocial relationships with YouTubers (three studies, 1,080+ participants)
evidence.finding: 52% report a strong parasocial relationship with a YouTuber; bonds grow with repeated exposure and self-address

evidence.source: Concept research of 9 Nov 2026 (handoff research digest): winners share a viewer stand-in, recurring characters and lore

items.title: Ideas sent to the Council must differ; a near-copy of an earlier idea is dropped
items.summary: AI help makes each single idea better but makes the set of ideas more alike. A creative run may send at most one proposal to the Council, inside the call it already makes; code drops one whose words overlap an earlier creative memo by half or more, so the Council chooses between real alternatives.

evidence.source: Doshi and Hauser, Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content, Science Advances 10(28)
evidence.finding: AI-assisted stories rated more creative but more similar to each other

items.title: B6a build takeaway: knowledge that was 'handed over' never reached a model - trace every rule to the call that uses it
items.summary: Before B6a every department 'took' its playbook and no model call ever saw it; 4 of the owner's own limits did not even fit the writer's block. Proof must sit where the work is made: the receipt names the calls that carried the knowledge, and a claim of use counts only with a quote code finds. Tests that play a lying model found what green runs hid.

evidence.source: v12 build, batch B6a (creative departments)
evidence.finding: All 15 departments ran in brief mode: take() was called and nothing read it. With PREPROD_ON the script was written outside any department run. Tests with a lying fake model found: any script line passed as the callback; every creative idea would have pinged the owner; the engine verified creative knowledge levers without a cited use. Mutations: removing verification fails 6 tests, removing the injection 9.
